input: # A byte-order mark, U+FEFF, at the start of the text is not part of the
# text: `parse` passes over it, under `strict` too, which RFC 8259 leaves
# to the reader. Only the TypeScript package does so under `strict` yet,
# so these rows are here and not in ../spec/ (see ../AGENTS.md, "Where a
# new fixture goes"). ../spec/raw-fast.tsv pins it for the default reader.
# Every input below opens with the mark, which is invisible.
# The checks of strict mode see the text without it.
# One mark is passed over. A second is text. To the default reader it
# starts a plain scalar, so the root of the first row is a string, and
# the member name of the second opens with the mark.
# Strict JSON refuses a second mark, as it does one anywhere else.
# A text that is the mark and nothing else has nothing in it.
# Under the specification's reading, as under the base one.
﻿openapi: 3.1.0\ninfo: {}\n
# Behind a mark, strict JSON is still strict: a trailing comma is refused.
# (The next input opens with a byte order mark, U+FEFF, which is invisible.)
